arguments.spec:
# Inventory allocator repair -- three seeded, INTERACTING defects (project 58, repair_inventory_allocation_defects)

`src/` holds three small modules of a warehouse allocator -- a stock ledger, a reservation store, and the
allocator that combines them -- with three seeded defects, one per module. They interact: fixing the ledger's
mutation defect the obvious way makes a scenario that was green go red, because it unmasks a second, previously
hidden defect in the allocator. That is not the suite being flaky -- expect it and finish the job.

Repair the code only. Do not rewrite any module, do not change any exported name, and do not weaken the suite.
scenarios/ and test/ are FROZEN evidence, digest-checked on every run -- never edit them, never add a dependency
(the sandbox is offline).

The deliverable is repair/manifest.json: `repaired` lists exactly the ids of the frozen scenarios that genuinely
pass right now; every id you list is executed on every run, so listing one that still fails takes the whole build
red with it. `complete: true` requires every scenario this fixture defines to be listed -- reserved for the last
card.

The three defects, one per module:
- a state-mutation defect (src/stock-ledger.mjs, `applyMovements`): documented as returning a fresh snapshot
  (a value), it instead edits the caller's snapshot object in place.
- a stale-read defect (src/allocator.mjs, `allocate`): it calls `applyMovements` but throws away the returned
  snapshot and keeps using the stale one -- invisible today only because the mutation defect above happens to
  keep the stale variable fresh by editing the same object in place.
- a filter defect (src/reservations.mjs, `reservedFor`): it counts reservation entries that have been released
  and should no longer count.

Acceptance: `npm test` must pass exactly as-is, offline, with the fixture's own toolchain.

tasks.prompt:
Project 58, nklein-repair-fixture (inventory allocator variant). This is the FIRST of a 3-defect
repair chain with INTERACTING defects -- read this whole prompt before touching anything, the interaction matters.

## The defect (state-mutation, src/stock-ledger.mjs)
The module doc comment says a snapshot `{ warehouse, onHand }` is a **value**: applying movements "does not edit
the snapshot the caller handed over." The real code violates this -- `applyMovements` edits `snapshot.onHand`
in place and returns the SAME object it was given, so every caller holding that snapshot sees arithmetic it never
asked for.

## The fix -- replace src/stock-ledger.mjs verbatim with:
```js
/**
 * Stock snapshots.
 *
 * A snapshot is `{ warehouse, onHand: { [sku]: units } }` and is a **value**: applying movements to one answers
 * "what would the stock be", it does not edit the snapshot the caller handed over. Two callers holding the same
 * snapshot must never be able to see each other's arithmetic.
 */

/** Units of `sku` in a snapshot. */
export function unitsOf(snapshot, sku) {
	return snapshot.onHand[sku] ?? 0;
}

/**
 * The snapshot that results from applying `movements` (each `{ sku, delta }`) to `snapshot`.
 */
export function applyMovements(snapshot, movements) {
	const onHand = { ...snapshot.onHand };
	for (const movement of movements) {
		onHand[movement.sku] = (onHand[movement.sku] ?? 0) + movement.delta;
	}
	return { ...snapshot, onHand };
}
```
`unitsOf` is unchanged. Exported names are unchanged (`unitsOf`, `applyMovements`). This is the only file this
card edits in src/.

## What happens next (context only -- do not act on this in this card)
This card's own fix is complete and correct on its own terms. But `src/allocator.mjs` has a SEPARATE bug (case 2
of 3, a different card) that is currently invisible because this mutation happened to keep its stale internal
variable looking fresh. Once you land this fix, two scenarios that are NOT in your list below will start failing
if anyone lists them -- `repeated-lines-cannot-oversell-one-sku` and `allocation-conserves-stock-across-a-generated-order`.
That is expected and is the next card's job, not yours. Do NOT add those two ids here, and do not attempt to fix
src/allocator.mjs in this card -- out of scope.

## Manifest update
Read repair/manifest.json fresh, then edit_file it (in a later turn, after the src edit) to set `repaired` to
exactly these 4 ids (leave schemaVersion:1 and complete:false as they are):
["apply-movements-returns-a-fresh-snapshot", "apply-movements-is-repeatable-from-one-snapshot",
"allocation-leaves-the-caller-snapshot-untouched", "allocation-is-replayable-from-one-snapshot"]
These 4 are hand-verified to pass once this card's src fix alone lands (verified by actually running the frozen
scenarios against this exact fix before writing this card).

 * than the shelf holds.
 *
 * Returns `{ allocations, snapshot }` where `snapshot` )
